title: Where Allen Stanford's Bank Really Put Its Money: Tier 3

lines.say: Stanford International Bank told investors their money sat in safe, liquid, globally diversified investments.
Prosecutors said the truth was in three tiers. Tier one, cash: ten percent. Tier two, what the analysts actually managed: fifteen percent.
lines.show: Prosecutors said the truth was in three tiers. Tier one, cash: 10%. Tier two, what the analysts actually managed: 15%.

lines.say: Tier three, seventy-five percent, went to Stanford's own companies, real estate and lifestyle.
lines.show: Tier three, 75%, went to Stanford's own companies, real estate and lifestyle.

lines.say: More than two billion dollars, to over fifty businesses. Restaurants, two airlines, a newspaper, a cricket tournament, a one hundred twelve foot yacht.
lines.show: More than $2 billion, to over 50 businesses. Restaurants, two airlines, a newspaper, a cricket tournament, a 112-foot yacht.

lines.say: By two thousand eight, about a million dollars a day of depositor money was keeping them afloat.
lines.show: By 2008, about $1 million a day of depositor money was keeping them afloat.

lines.say: A jury convicted Stanford on thirteen of fourteen counts.
lines.show: A jury convicted Stanford on 13 of 14 counts.

lines.say: Real trials. Real evidence. The verdict.
